# REST API: OAuth App resource

---

An OAuth App resource represents an [account-level OAuth app](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/account-oauth-apps). Use the OAuth App resource to create and manage OAuth apps and rotate their client secrets.

(information)

## Note

The OAuth App resource only supports account OAuth apps that use the Client Credentials grant type. To generate an access token with an OAuth app's credentials, use the [OAuth Token API](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/oauth-access-token).

All requests use the base URL `https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps`.

You can authenticate requests using either HTTP Basic authentication or OAuth.

For HTTP Basic authentication, use your Account SID and Auth Token or an [API key](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/api-keys) SID and secret.

For OAuth, send an access token from the [OAuth Token API](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/oauth-access-token) as a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header.

If your request includes a body, it must be formatted as JSON.

---

## OAuth App properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sid` | string | The unique identifier of the OAuth app, which is also its client ID. Starts with `OQ`. |
| `type` | string | The OAuth grant type of the OAuth app, which is always `Client Credential`. |
| `friendly_name` | string | The name of the OAuth app. |
| `description` | string | A description of the OAuth app. |
| `status` | string | The status of the OAuth app, for example `ACTIVE`. |
| `policy` | object | The permissions granted to the OAuth app. See [Policy object](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/account-oauth-apps-resource#policy-object). |
| `access_token_ttl` | integer | The length of time in minutes that access tokens issued for the OAuth app remain valid. |
| `date_created` | string | The date and time the OAuth app was created, in ISO 8601 format. |
| `created_by` | string | The email address of the user who created the OAuth app. |
| `creator_sid` | string | The SID of the user who created the OAuth app. Starts with `US`. |
| `secret` | string | The client secret of the OAuth app. Returned when you create, update, or rotate the secret of an OAuth app. Not returned when you fetch or list OAuth apps. |

### Policy object

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `allow` | array of strings | The permissions the OAuth app can use, for example `/twilio/messaging/messages/read`. |

(warning)

## Warning

An account OAuth app can have up to 100 permissions in `policy.allow`. Wildcards, such as `/twilio/messaging/*`, aren't allowed, so each entry must be an explicit permission. See [Scopes/Permissions available for OAuth apps](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/account-oauth-apps#scopespermissions-available-for-oauth-apps).

---

## Create an OAuth App resource

`POST https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps`

Create an OAuth app.

**Encoding type**: `application/json`

#### Request body parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | yes | The OAuth grant type of the OAuth app. Must be `Client Credential`. |
| `owner_sid` | string | yes | The SID of the account that owns the OAuth app. Must match the account you authenticate with. |
| `friendly_name` | string | yes | The name of the OAuth app. Maximum 64 characters. |
| `description` | string | no | A description of the OAuth app. Maximum 140 characters. |
| `policy` | object | yes | The permissions to grant the OAuth app. `policy.allow` must contain at least one permission. See [Policy object](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/account-oauth-apps-resource#policy-object). |
| `access_token_ttl` | integer | no | The length of time in minutes that access tokens remain valid. Maximum 43200 (30 days). Defaults to 60 (1 hour). |
| `token_endpoint_auth_method` | string | no | How the OAuth app authenticates when it requests an access token. The only supported value is `client_secret_basic`. |

```
1curl -X POST "https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps" \
2-u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN \
3-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
4-d '{
5    "type": "Client Credential",
6    "owner_sid": "ACXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
7    "friendly_name": "My OAuth App",
8    "description": "Sends messages from my backend service",
9    "policy": {
10        "allow": ["/twilio/messaging/messages/create", "/twilio/messaging/messages/read"]
11    },
12    "access_token_ttl": 60
13}'
```

If the request succeeds, Twilio returns `201 Created` with the new OAuth App resource.

```
1{
2    "type": "Client Credential",
3    "sid": "OQXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
4    "friendly_name": "My OAuth App",
5    "description": "Sends messages from my backend service",
6    "date_created": "2026-06-15T12:00:00Z",
7    "created_by": "user@example.com",
8    "creator_sid": "USXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
9    "secret": "{CLIENT_SECRET}",
10    "status": "ACTIVE",
11    "policy": {
12        "allow": ["/twilio/messaging/messages/create", "/twilio/messaging/messages/read"]
13    },
14    "access_token_ttl": 60
15}
```

(warning)

## Warning

Keep your OAuth app secure by storing the `secret` in a secrets manager, such as AWS Secrets Manager or HashiCorp Vault, as soon as you receive it. Never hard-code it or commit it to version control. Fetch and list responses don't include the secret. If you lose it or it's exposed, [rotate the secret](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/account-oauth-apps-resource#rotate-the-secret-of-an-oauth-app-resource).

---

## Fetch an OAuth App resource

`GET https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps/{sid}`

Retrieve an OAuth app. For security reasons, the response doesn't include the `secret`.

#### Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sid` | string | yes | The SID of the OAuth app to fetch. Starts with `OQ`. |

```
1curl -X GET "https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps/OQXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" \
2-u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
```

If the request succeeds, Twilio returns `200 OK` with the OAuth App resource.

```
1{
2    "type": "Client Credential",
3    "sid": "OQXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
4    "friendly_name": "My OAuth App",
5    "description": "Sends messages from my backend service",
6    "date_created": "2026-06-15T12:00:00Z",
7    "created_by": "user@example.com",
8    "creator_sid": "USXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
9    "status": "ACTIVE",
10    "policy": {
11        "allow": ["/twilio/messaging/messages/create", "/twilio/messaging/messages/read"]
12    },
13    "access_token_ttl": 60
14}
```

---

## List OAuth App resources

`GET https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps`

Retrieve a list of OAuth apps that belong to the account you authenticate with.

```
1curl -X GET "https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps" \
2-u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
```

If the request succeeds, Twilio returns `200 OK` with the OAuth App resources in the `content` array.

```
1{
2    "content": [
3        {
4            "type": "Client Credential",
5            "sid": "OQXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
6            "friendly_name": "My OAuth App",
7            "description": "Sends messages from my backend service",
8            "date_created": "2026-06-15T12:00:00Z",
9            "created_by": "user@example.com",
10            "creator_sid": "USXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
11            "status": "ACTIVE",
12            "policy": {
13                "allow": ["/twilio/messaging/messages/create", "/twilio/messaging/messages/read"]
14            },
15            "access_token_ttl": 60
16        }
17    ]
18}
```

---

## Update an OAuth App resource

`PUT https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps/{sid}`

Update an OAuth app. Only the fields you include in the request change.

**Encoding type**: `application/json`

#### Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sid` | string | yes | The SID of the OAuth app to update. Starts with `OQ`. |

#### Request body parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `friendly_name` | string | no | The name of the OAuth app. Maximum 64 characters. |
| `description` | string | no | A description of the OAuth app. Maximum 140 characters. |
| `policy` | object | no | The permissions to grant the OAuth app. See [Policy object](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/account-oauth-apps-resource#policy-object). |
| `access_token_ttl` | integer | no | The length of time in minutes that access tokens remain valid. Maximum 43200 (30 days). |

(warning)

## Update the policy

The update request completely overwrites the existing policy of the OAuth app. Include all the permissions the OAuth app needs in the `policy` object. To remove a permission while keeping others, include only the permissions to keep.

```
1curl -X PUT "https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps/OQXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" \
2-u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN \
3-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
4-d '{
5    "friendly_name": "My Updated OAuth App",
6    "description": "Updated description",
7    "access_token_ttl": 120
8}'
```

If the request succeeds, Twilio returns `200 OK` with the updated OAuth App resource, including its current `secret`.

```
1{
2    "type": "Client Credential",
3    "sid": "OQXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
4    "friendly_name": "My Updated OAuth App",
5    "description": "Updated description",
6    "date_created": "2026-06-15T12:00:00Z",
7    "created_by": "user@example.com",
8    "creator_sid": "USXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
9    "secret": "{CLIENT_SECRET}",
10    "status": "ACTIVE",
11    "policy": {
12        "allow": ["/twilio/messaging/messages/create", "/twilio/messaging/messages/read"]
13    },
14    "access_token_ttl": 120
15}
```

---

## Delete an OAuth App resource

`DELETE https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps/{sid}`

Delete an OAuth app. After deletion, you can't generate access tokens with the OAuth app's credentials.

(warning)

## OAuth app deletion is permanent and can't be undone

Deleting an OAuth app also invalidates all access tokens issued for it. If you only need to address compromised credentials, [rotate the client secret](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/account-oauth-apps-resource#rotate-the-secret-of-an-oauth-app-resource) instead of deleting the OAuth app.

#### Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sid` | string | yes | The SID of the OAuth app to delete. Starts with `OQ`. |

```
1curl -X DELETE "https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps/OQXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" \
2-u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
```

If the request succeeds, Twilio returns `204 No Content` with no body.

---

## Rotate the secret of an OAuth App resource

`POST https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps/{sid}/secret`

Generate a new client secret for an OAuth app. You can set `gracePeriodInSeconds` to keep the old secret valid while you roll out the new one.

#### Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sid` | string | yes | The SID of the OAuth app whose secret to rotate. Starts with `OQ`. |

#### Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gracePeriodInSeconds` | integer | no | The length of time in seconds that the old secret remains valid. Must be between 0 and 2678400. If set to 0, the old secret becomes invalid immediately. |

```
1curl -X POST "https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps/OQXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX/secret?gracePeriodInSeconds=86400" \
2-u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
```

If the request succeeds, Twilio returns `200 OK` with the OAuth App resource, including the new `secret`.

```
1{
2    "type": "Client Credential",
3    "sid": "OQXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
4    "friendly_name": "My OAuth App",
5    "description": "Sends messages from my backend service",
6    "date_created": "2026-06-15T12:00:00Z",
7    "created_by": "user@example.com",
8    "creator_sid": "USXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
9    "secret": "{NEW_CLIENT_SECRET}",
10    "status": "ACTIVE",
11    "policy": {
12        "allow": ["/twilio/messaging/messages/create", "/twilio/messaging/messages/read"]
13    },
14    "access_token_ttl": 60
15}
```

---

## Errors

If a request fails, Twilio returns a JSON error body with `code`, `message`, `more_info`, and `status` fields.

| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| `400` | The request is invalid. For example, a field exceeds its maximum length, the policy is empty or contains a wildcard, or `gracePeriodInSeconds` is out of range. |
| `401` | The request isn't authenticated. |
| `403` | The credentials don't have permission to perform this action. |
| `404` | The OAuth app doesn't exist or has been deleted. |
